title: Riffle benchlet — personal micro-run ledger
content_plain:
One-page working ledger for quick micro-runs. Purpose: capture fast iterations on batching + KV-cache heuristics for short conversational sequences (<=256). Not polished — notes to self, guesses, and immediate takeaways. Use this to pick 2–3 candidates for more formal sweep.

Quick context: testing small-batch behavior for 7B quantized variant on T4-like instance with prefix caching turned on/off. Looking for p99 < 120ms for batch_size 8 and acceptable cost per 1k tokens.

Questions I want answered here:
- Does prefix caching help for mixed seq_len spikes (32/128)?
- When does continuous batching start hurting p99?
- Which quant profile gives best latency/cost tradeoff for short convo flows?

Notes to self: copy best rows into central spreadsheet after thresholding latency and cost. Tag runs with RIF- for riffle experiments.

freeform_notes:
Quick observations:
- Prefix/KV caching is the single largest lever for reducing p99 in short convos — keep on by default for hosted slow-starts.
- 4-bit gives decent unit cost but more variance at longer seq lengths; consider hybrid policy: int8 for seq_len>64, 4-bit for <=32.
- Continuous batching seems helpful up to batch 6 for these models; beyond that tail latency climbs nonlinearly.

Scratch TODO (non-blocking): try small run with model-splitting fallback to cheaper variant if p99 > 200ms (simulate overload).
